note: RIDDLER SEAT 3 — the anthropologist. Riddle: the strange made familiar until you cannot say which it was. Roads, thresholds, clerks. Equivalents ride this shelf (Calvino, Saramago, Butler, Chiang). Everything walled; lens carried by quotation.
interactions: father Alfred Kroeber: the anthropologist who received Ishi; Always Coming Home (1985) is Kroeber's method turned into fiction
'The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas' (1973) cites William James' moral-philosophy experiment by name
'On Fairy-Stories' → Earthsea: the dragons-and-consolation inheritance from the tolkien shelf, then corrected in Tehanu
Lao Tzu: Tao Te Ching translation (1997) — water as the highest good is the clerk's cousin
2014 National Book Awards speech revived Orwell's suppressed Animal Farm preface on 'the freedom of the press' (edge: orwell shelf)
walled: Earthsea: A Wizard of Earthsea (1968); The Tombs of Atuan (1971); The Farthest Shore (1972); Tehanu (1990); Tales from Earthsea (2001); The Other Wind (2001)

Hainish: Rocannon's World (1966); Planet of Exile (1966); City of Illusions (1967); The Left Hand of Darkness (1969); The Word for World Is Forest (1972); The Dispossessed (1974); Four Ways to Forgiveness (1995); The Telling (2000)
standalone: The Lathe of Heaven (1971); The Eye of the Heron; Always Coming Home (1985); The Beginning Place; Annals of the Western Shore (Gifts, Voices, Powers); Lavinia (2008)
stories: The Wind's Twelve Quarters (1975); The Compass Rose (1982); A Fisherman of the Inland Sea; 'The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas' (1973); 'The Day Before the Revolution'

essays: The Language of the Night (1979); Dancing at the Edge of the World (1989); The Wave in the Mind (2004); Steering the Craft (1998); Conversations on Writing (2018); No Time to Spare (2017); the 2014 National Book Awards speech
translation: Lao Tzu, Tao Te Ching (1997)

Calvino: Invisible Cities (1972/74); If on a winter's night a traveler (1979/81); Cosmicomics (1965/68); t zero; The Baron in the Trees (1957); Mr. Palomar (1983/85); Six Memos for the Next Millennium (1988/93); Italian Folktales (1956/80); The Road to San Giovanni
Saramago: Blindness (1995/97); Seeing; Death with Interruptions (2005/08); The Gospel According to Jesus Christ (1991/93); All the Names; Baltasar and Blimunda; Essay on Blindness

Butler: Kindred (1979); the Patternist series (1976-84) incl. Wild Seed; the Xenogenesis trilogy / Lilith's Brood (1987-89); Parable of the Sower (1993); Parable of the Talents (1998); Bloodchild (1995); Fledgling (2005)

Chiang: Stories of Your Life and Others (2002) incl. 'Tower of Babylon', 'Understand', 'Story of Your Life', 'Hell Is the Absence of God'; Exhalation (2019) incl. 'The Merchant and the Alchemist's Gate', 'Lifecycle of Software Objects', 'Omphalos', 'Anxiety Is the Dizziness of Freedom'

equivalents.calvino: the anthropologist of impossible cities; exactitude plus lightness
equivalents.saramago: the anthropologist without punctuation; the whole town is the protagonist
equivalents.butler: the anthropologist of power and kinship; history as biology you cannot opt out of
equivalents.chiang: the anthropologist of thought experiments; every story a proof, every proof a grief
